info.title: threads host API
info.description: The typed HTTP/JSON API of host(). Every route under /v1 is a thin wrapper over the library method named in x-api; its x-error-codes are that method's typed failures plus the HTTP ones. Bodies are defined in host-api.v1.schema.json. Callers are authenticated as principals by host({authenticate}); without authenticate every /v1 route answers 401. Host contract: every create, read and mutation is scoped to the authenticated principal's tenant (another tenant's thread is not_found); a branch_id must belong to the thread in the path or body; and the host always passes the authenticated principal to the library call, never the local-operator default that agent.run() uses without a host. Each route's error bodies are a Failure whose code is exactly that route's x-error-codes. Status: 400 invalid_request, 401 unauthenticated, 403 forbidden, 404 not_found, 409 any domain code.

host.description: Checked by host({authenticate}), which maps the request to a Principal or rejects it.

idempotency_key.name: Idempotency-Key
idempotency_key.description: Stored atomically with the accepted user_input, bound to the tenant, the full authenticated principal (issuer, tenant, subject), the operation and the body hash. The same key, principal and body replays the same receipt and starts nothing; a different body is idempotency_key_reused (409); a different principal in the same tenant is idempotency_key_principal_mismatch (409) and never sees the other receipt.

UiRunError.description: Typed failure of the UI start-and-stream routes, before any stream starts. After it has started, a failure is a protocol error frame.

UiReconnectError.description: Typed failure of the AI SDK reconnect route.

UiCursorError.description: Typed failure of the committed-frames UI route.

AgUiContentPart.description: A part of a user message's content: text is read, any other type is refused.

AgUiMessage.description: One AG-UI message. Only the last user message is read, as the run's input.

AgUiResumeEntry.description: An answer to one interrupt: resolved with a payload (an ApprovalDecision or an Answer), or cancelled.

AgUiRunInput.description: POST /v1/ui/ag-ui/{agent}: the part of an AG-UI 1.0 RunAgentInput that threads reads. state, context and forwardedProps are ignored; a non-empty tools is refused.

AiSdkApproval.description: A tool part's approval: id is the challenge_id; approved and reason are the browser's decision.

AiSdkChatRequest.description: POST /v1/ui/ai-sdk/{agent}: the part of an AI SDK 7 chat request (DefaultChatTransport's body) that threads reads. Other keys, and other fields of messages and parts, are ignored: the browser's history is never read as truth.

AiSdkMessage.description: One UIMessage. Only the last one is read: a user message starts a run, an assistant message carries approval decisions and ask_user answers.

AiSdkPart.description: One UIMessage part: text (type text), or a tool part (type tool-<name>) with its state, approval and output.

Answer.description: The answer to an ask_user question: text, or the chosen options.

remember_rule.description: grant only: appended as permission_rule_added. Must be one of the challenge's suggested_rules.

runnable.description: false for an inspection-only repair branch.

ChatKey.description: A browser's conversation id on the UI routes (AI SDK useChat({id}), AG-UI threadId). With the signed-in principal and the agent it names one thread (spec/schema/ui/README.md, "Chat key"). Never recorded.

ErrorBody.description: Every non-2xx JSON response of the host API.

Failure.description: The error half of every expected-failure result.

event_id.description: The snapshot event: the value fork() takes.

mode.description: stub: no mediated operation goes live. Default live.

Input.description: What a run starts with: plain text or ordered input parts.

ParkedResolution.description: A human settling an unknown effect (C3). Recorded as effect_resolved{by: human}.

suggested_rules.description: Rules the approver may keep for this thread.

reason.description: Why the call asks, copied from its permission_decision: a hook's rule, or the memory_write option to change.

member.description: In a team member's thread: which member, as its starter's member_started records it, with the label and, for a dynamic agent, what the starter chose (define). Absent in any other thread.

RunAccepted.description: The receipt of POST /v1/runs and Host.startRun: the user_input is durable. run_id is that user_input's event_id, the run's durable identity. A replay under the same Idempotency-Key returns the same receipt.

RunErrorCode.description: RunResult failed.error.code, closed. stop_hook_limit is the pinned turn_completed reason; model_error is turn_completed{error}.

RunOutcome.description: RunResult as data (the HTTP form). The library RunResult carries a Thread handle where this carries ids.

output.description: The accepted structured output, or the final text when the agent has no output schema.

SettingsChange.description: An operator settings change. The host resolves model to the model factory named in the agent's model or fallback list; adapter settings come from that factory.

SseMessage.description: The data of one SSE message on a run subscription: a StreamEvent, then one final result message naming the run when it ends.

thread_id.description: Continue this thread. Absent: a new thread.

branch_id.description: With thread_id: the branch to continue. Absent: the thread's main branch.

budget.description: Run budget, recorded on the user_input; covers the whole agent tree.

StreamEvent.description: One item of stream() and of the SSE stream. event: a committed log event (durable). delta and status are transient and never logged.

entries.description: The resolved chain, oldest first (ancestor segments, then this branch).

TimelineEntry.description: One step of timeline() (F13.1). model_request events carry request_ref, the exact bytes the model saw.

fork_point.description: true for an eligible snapshot event.

ag-ui-1.title: AG-UI Protocol
ag-ui-1.description: The machine-readable contract for the AG-UI protocol. Validating a document against this file validates it as an AG-UI event; every other definition is addressable by its own anchor, so this file's own address followed by #RunAgentInput names the request body. Addresses are written relative to $id rather than spelled out, so a frozen copy of this file describes itself rather than the draft it came from. Field names are camelCase because this describes the wire format rather than any language's idiom. Objects are exact: this file defines what exists in this version of the protocol, so a property it does not declare fails validation. Compatibility with newer minor versions is a behavioural rule for receivers, who tolerate what they do not recognise rather than rejecting it; a validator has no way to express tolerance, so that rule lives in the prose specification. How events may be ordered and whether a patch applies to the state it targets are behavioural rules for the same reason. Exactness has three kinds of exception: the compositional fragments — BaseEvent, Attributable, BaseMessage — which are open in themselves because the definitions composing them close the whole shape; objects that are open by meaning, because arbitrary keys are their data rather than unrecognised fields — metadata, activity content, a carried JSON Schema — and the JSON Patch operations, which stay open because RFC 6902 requires members an operation does not define to be ignored rather than rejected.

ag-ui-1_ActivityDeltaEvent.description: Changes an activity message's content incrementally.

activityType.description: What kind of activity this is.

patch.description: The change, as an RFC 6902 patch against the activity's content.

ag-ui-1_ActivityMessage.description: Structured progress that is not conversation content, materialised as a message so it keeps its place in the sequence. Stands alone rather than composing BaseMessage, because its content is an object rather than a string.

role.description: Fixed. Declared here rather than inherited, because this message does not compose BaseMessage.

activityType.description: What kind of activity this is. An open string: the set is the producer's.

content.description: The activity's payload, open by key.

metadata.description: Extra information attached to this message.

ag-ui-1_ActivitySnapshotEvent.description: Reports structured progress that is not conversation content, such as a step a UI renders as its own widget.

activityType.description: What kind of activity this is. An open string: the set is the producer's, not the protocol's.

content.description: The activity's payload, open by key.

replace.description: Whether this snapshot overwrites the activity's existing content. Absent means it does, and that meaning is normative; only an explicit false asks a consumer to leave what is already there. It does not ask for a merge — ACTIVITY_DELTA is how content is changed incrementally. What a consumer does with a non-overwriting snapshot is behavioural and belongs in the prose.

ag-ui-1_AddOperation.description: Inserts value at path. RFC 6902 section 4.1.

value.description: The value to insert. Any JSON value, including null, which is a legitimate thing to add.

ag-ui-1_AssistantMessage.description: A message from the agent. Content is optional because a turn may consist only of tool calls.

content.description: What the agent said, if it said anything.

toolCalls.description: The tool calls this turn made.

ag-ui-1_Attributable.description: Composed into everything that can belong to a subagent's work: the events that describe content or progress, the message types, and each interrupt. Run-scoped events omit it — RUN_STARTED, RUN_FINISHED and RUN_ERROR describe the run itself and MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT is conversation-wide, so none of them can belong to one subagent. A tool call omits it too and inherits its containing message's attribution.

subagentRunId.description: The subagent invocation this belongs to. Absent means the parent agent produced it directly.

id.description: Identifies this part within its message. Optional, and nothing reads it yet: reserved as on the text part.

metadata.description: Extra information about this part. Unconstrained, as on the other media parts.

ag-ui-1_BaseEvent.description: The fields every event carries, whatever its type. Composed into each event definition rather than repeated, so a change here reaches every event at once.

type.description: Which event this is. Each event definition narrows this to a single value.

timestamp.description: When the event was created. Bounded to the range JSON numbers survive a round trip in, so the value a consumer reads is the value the producer wrote. Deliberately not a float. The unit is not constrained here, because it never has been stated normatively; every SDK that sets it in practice uses milliseconds since the Unix epoch, and a producer choosing another unit will be misread by consumers even though it validates. Nothing in the protocol computes with this value.

rawEvent.description: The provider-native event this one was translated from, carried verbatim for debugging and for consumers that need detail the protocol does not model. Any JSON value.

metadata.description: Extra information attached to this event.

ag-ui-1_BaseMessage.description: The fields shared by the developer, system, assistant and user messages. Deliberately excludes content, because a user message's content may be an array while the others are strings, and composition here intersects rather than overrides: a base that constrained content to a string would make an array content invalid. The tool, activity and reasoning messages do not compose this, because they carry no name.

id.description: Identifies the message within the conversation.

role.description: Who the message is from. Each message definition narrows this to a single value.

name.description: An optional display name for the author.

encryptedValue.description: A provider's opaque artefact belonging to this message, stored by a consumer and returned on a later turn.

metadata.description: Extra information attached to this message.

ag-ui-1_ContentPart.description: One part of a message body: what a person sends in a user message, or what a tool returns in a tool message. Discriminated by type. Named by what the part is rather than by direction, because the same part travels into the model inside a user message and back out of the stream inside a tool result.

ag-ui-1_Context.description: A named piece of ambient information given to the agent for the run, distinct from the conversation.

description.description: What this context is, for the agent to interpret.

ag-ui-1_CopyOperation.description: Copies the value at from to path. RFC 6902 section 4.5.

from.description: Where the value is copied from.

path.description: Where the value is copied to.

ag-ui-1_CustomEvent.description: The protocol's extension point for an application's own events. Anything a consumer does with one is outside the protocol.

name.description: What this custom event is. Required: without it a consumer cannot route the value.

value.description: The payload. Any JSON value, and required.
The bytes, base64-encoded. contentEncoding is an annotation rather than a constraint in 2020-12, so a malformed string still validates here; rejecting one is the decoder's job.

mimeType.description: What the bytes are. Required here, unlike on a URL source, because nothing else can tell a consumer how to read them.

content.description: The instructions. Required: a developer message with nothing in it says nothing.

id.description: Identifies this part within its message. Optional, and nothing reads it yet: reserved as on the text part.

metadata.description: Extra information about this part. Unconstrained, as on the other media parts.

ag-ui-1_Event.description: Any AG-UI event. Every member is normative: there is no optional tier and no event a consumer may decline to implement. Discriminated by the type property.

ag-ui-1_EventType.description: The discriminator carried by every event.

ag-ui-1_FileSource.description: Bytes already at the provider, named by a handle the provider issued: an OpenAI or Anthropic file id, a Gemini file URI, a storage URL only that provider can read. No bytes travel and nothing is fetched. Only the provider that minted the handle can resolve it; a peer that cannot drops the part as it drops any part it cannot use.

value.description: The handle, exactly as the provider issued it. Opaque: a consumer MUST NOT fetch it, parse it or read a scheme out of it.

provider.description: Who issued the handle, when the producer knows. Optional: an agent already knows which provider it talks to. When present, SHOULD be the lowercase vendor id (openai, anthropic, google) that TokenUsage.provider uses, so a peer can tell before sending whether a handle is one it can use.

mimeType.description: What the file is, when the producer knows. Optional, because the provider that holds the bytes knows.

ag-ui-1_FunctionCall.description: The name and arguments of a tool call.

arguments.description: The arguments as a JSON string, not as parsed JSON. Kept as written because a model can emit arguments that are not valid JSON, and losing them at the protocol boundary would hide the fault from the consumer that has to handle it.

id.description: Identifies this part within its message. Optional, and nothing reads it yet: reserved as on the text part.

metadata.description: Extra information about this part. Unconstrained rather than an object: inherited from the SDKs, which declare it unknown rather than a record; listed under known divergences in the README rather than resolved here.

ag-ui-1_Interrupt.description: Something a run needs from outside before it can continue, such as an approval or a missing value.

id.description: Identifies the interrupt. A resume entry answers it by this id.

reason.description: Why the run stopped. An open string rather than an enumeration: the protocol does not attempt to classify every reason an agent might need input.

message.description: A human-readable prompt for whoever answers.

toolCallId.description: The tool call this interrupt concerns, when it is a tool approval.

responseSchema.description: A JSON Schema describing the answer this interrupt expects, so a consumer can build a form for it. Carried opaquely: the protocol does not constrain or validate it. Restricted to an object because TypeScript and Python both declare it that way; .NET holds it as any JSON, and the ticket that commissioned this schema lists it among the arbitrary-JSON fields. Following the two that constrain it keeps the schema from accepting documents the reference client rejects, at the cost of rejecting the boolean schemas JSON Schema also permits — a bare true for "any answer". Recorded as a known divergence rather than settled.

expiresAt.description: When the interrupt stops being answerable. Deliberately unconstrained rather than a date-time format, because producers already disagree about the representation and tightening it here would reject streams that work today. The documented convention is ISO 8601, and a consumer comparing this value will parse it as a date, so a value that is not one leaves the interrupt looking permanently unexpired.

metadata.description: Extra information attached to this interrupt.

ag-ui-1_JsonPatch.description: A JSON Patch document as defined by RFC 6902, referenced by STATE_DELTA.delta and ACTIVITY_DELTA.patch: an ordered sequence of operations applied to a target document. An empty array is a valid no-op patch. Whether the operations actually apply to the document they target is a runtime question RFC 6902 leaves to the applier; structural validity here says nothing about it.

ag-ui-1_JsonPatchOperation.description: A single RFC 6902 operation. Exactly one of the operation shapes must match, discriminated by op. Unlike the protocol's own objects, the operations are open: RFC 6902 section 4 requires members an operation does not define to be ignored rather than rejected, so a remove carrying a leftover value is a valid patch. Two of the RFC's rules are relations between values rather than shapes, so no static schema can express them and neither is checked here: a move whose from is a proper prefix of its path (section 4.4), and any operation whose pointer does not resolve in the target document. Both are the applier's to reject.

ag-ui-1_JsonPointer.description: A JSON Pointer as defined by RFC 6901. Either the empty string, meaning the whole document, or a sequence of slash-prefixed reference tokens in which a tilde is escaped as ~0 and a slash as ~1. A value with no leading slash, or a tilde followed by anything other than 0 or 1, is not a JSON Pointer.

ag-ui-1_Message.description: Any message in a conversation. Discriminated by role.

ag-ui-1_MessagesSnapshotEvent.description: The complete set of messages the producer owns, in order. Conversation-wide rather than a plain overwrite: a consumer may keep messages of its own that no producer tracks, so exactly how a snapshot reconciles with those is behavioural and belongs in the prose. Being conversation-wide it cannot belong to a single subagent, so it carries no attribution; it does establish which subagent owns each message it contains, through the messages themselves.

messages.description: The messages the producer is declaring, in order.

ag-ui-1_Metadata.description: Extra information attached to an event, a message, a tool call, a tool, an interrupt or a resume entry. Open by key: any JSON value is allowed under a key, including null, because a null there is meaningful data. The object itself may be absent but is never null when present. The key ag-ui is reserved for the protocol's own use; reservation is by convention, since validating the shape of a key's value would contradict being open by key.

ag-ui-1_MoveOperation.description: Moves the value at from to path. RFC 6902 section 4.4.

from.description: Where the value is moved from.

path.description: Where the value is moved to.

ag-ui-1_PartSource.description: Where a media part's bytes come from: carried inline, referenced by URL, or already at the provider under a handle it issued.

ag-ui-1_RawEvent.description: Passes a provider-native event through untranslated, for consumers that need detail the protocol does not model.

event.description: The provider's own event. Any JSON value, and required: an event whose only purpose is to carry this would say nothing without it.

source.description: Which provider or framework the event came from.

ag-ui-1_ReasoningEncryptedValueEvent.description: Carries a provider's opaque, encrypted reasoning artefact, which a consumer stores and returns on a later turn without being able to read it.

subtype.description: What kind of thing entityId names, which decides where the value is stored.

entityId.description: What the value belongs to: a message id or a tool call id, according to subtype.

ag-ui-1_ReasoningEncryptedValueSubtype.description: Whether a REASONING_ENCRYPTED_VALUE belongs to a message or to a tool call.

ag-ui-1_ReasoningMessage.description: A span of the agent's reasoning, materialised as a message. Stands alone rather than composing BaseMessage, because it carries no name.

role.description: Fixed. Declared here rather than inherited, because this message does not compose BaseMessage.

encryptedValue.description: A provider's opaque reasoning artefact belonging to this message.

metadata.description: Extra information attached to this message.

ag-ui-1_ReasoningMessageChunkEvent.description: A shorthand that stands in for a reasoning message's start, content and end sequence.

messageId.description: The reasoning message this chunk belongs to. Absent continues the one already open.

delta.description: The fragment to append. May be the empty string.

ag-ui-1_ReasoningMessageContentEvent.description: Appends a fragment to a streamed reasoning message.

messageId.description: The reasoning message this fragment belongs to.

delta.description: The fragment to append. May be the empty string.

messageId.description: The reasoning message this stream builds.

role.description: Fixed, and required rather than defaulted. The requirement is inherited from the SDKs rather than chosen.

ag-ui-1_ReasoningStartEvent.description: Opens a span of reasoning. A span may contain several reasoning messages.

ag-ui-1_RemoveOperation.description: Removes the value at path. RFC 6902 section 4.2.

ag-ui-1_ReplaceOperation.description: Replaces the value at path. RFC 6902 section 4.3.

value.description: The replacement. Any JSON value, including null.

ag-ui-1_ResumeEntry.description: An answer to one interrupt, sent on the run that continues from it.

status.description: Whether the interrupt was answered or abandoned.

payload.description: The answer the agent asked for and will act on. Any JSON value.

metadata.description: Envelope information about the response, such as signatures or routing keys, as opposed to payload, which is the answer itself.

ag-ui-1_RunAgentInput.description: A request to run an agent. Also echoed back as RUN_STARTED.input. Only threadId, runId and messages are required: those are the three the SDKs already agree on, and for tools and context an absent key and an empty array mean the same thing, so requiring them would catch nothing a producer could get wrong.

threadId.description: The conversation this run belongs to.

protocolVersion.description: The protocol version this consumer speaks, such as "1.0". Absent means the input was produced before the protocol carried a version — the versioning rules in the prose govern what each side does with that. Sent in-band rather than by the transport, so a recorded exchange stays self-describing.

parentRunId.description: The run that spawned this one.

state.description: The state the run starts from.

messages.description: The conversation so far, in order.

tools.description: The tools the agent may call. Absent means none.

context.description: Ambient information for the run. Absent means none.

forwardedProps.description: Application-specific values passed through to the agent untouched. Any JSON value.

resume.description: Answers to the interrupts that ended a previous run, when this run continues from one.

ag-ui-1_RunErrorEvent.description: Ends a run that failed. Run-scoped, so it carries no subagent attribution; a subagent that fails without ending the run reports SUBAGENT_ERROR instead.

message.description: What went wrong, for a person to read.

code.description: A machine-readable error code. An open string: the protocol defines no vocabulary.

usage.description: Token usage accrued before the failure, for a run that completed one or more model calls before dying. Scoped as on RUN_FINISHED: the run's own calls, subagents included.

ag-ui-1_RunFinishedCancelledOutcome.description: The run was stopped before it completed, by whoever was running it, and did not fail. Neither success nor interrupt: nothing was produced as a result, and nothing is waited for, so the next run on the thread is an ordinary new run rather than a resume. Closed like its siblings: a cancelled run has no interrupts to carry. Named in the schema before 1.0 because an outcome a consumer does not recognise is stripped and read as success — a cancellation added later would reach every 1.0 consumer as a completed run.

ag-ui-1_RunFinishedEvent.description: Closes a run that did not fail. Run-scoped, so it carries no subagent attribution.

threadId.description: The conversation this run belongs to.

result.description: The run's return value, if it has one. Any JSON value.

outcome.description: Why the run ended. Absent means success, so every producer written before outcomes existed is already conformant.

usage.description: Token usage for the run, one entry per provider and model, so a run that invoked several models keeps them separate. A consumer that only wants totals sums across the entries. The run is the accounting boundary: usage covers every model call made within the run, calls made by its subagents included; an agent invoked as a separate run under parentRunId reports its own usage on its own terminal event; and a run that resumes an interrupted one reports only the calls it made itself, not the interrupted run's.

ag-ui-1_RunFinishedInterruptOutcome.description: The run is paused, waiting for something outside it. Resuming means starting a new run whose resume entries answer these interrupts.

interrupts.description: What the run is waiting for. At least one: an interrupt outcome with nothing to answer would leave a consumer with nothing to do.

ag-ui-1_RunFinishedSuccessOutcome.description: The run completed. Equivalent to an absent outcome. Closed like every other object, which is also what keeps it from carrying the suspended sibling's interrupts — a success with an interrupt still pending would be a contradiction, not an extension. A completed run may still have left frontend tool calls for the application to answer; pendingToolCallIds names them.

pendingToolCallIds.description: The tool calls this run started and left unanswered — no TOOL_CALL_RESULT in the run — for the application to answer in the next input's messages, in the order they were made. Absent or empty means the producer named none, and a consumer derives the list from the stream; otherwise it is the list, and it agrees with the stream. On the success outcome rather than the event because a run that stopped on a frontend tool call is a completed run: whether the application continues the thread is its own decision, so the producer reports what it knows and no more.

items.description: A tool call id, as carried by TOOL_CALL_START.

ag-ui-1_RunStartedEvent.description: Opens a run. Run-scoped, so it carries no subagent attribution.

threadId.description: The conversation this run belongs to.

protocolVersion.description: The protocol version this producer speaks, such as "1.0" — the producer's own version, not an echo of the input's, which is what makes the pair a negotiation: each side declares itself and the consumer sees a downgrade the moment it happens. Absent means a producer from before the protocol carried a version.

parentRunId.description: The run that spawned this one, when an agent invokes another agent as a separate run rather than as a subagent within one.

input.description: The request this run was started from, echoed back so a consumer that did not make the request can still see what the agent was asked.

ag-ui-1_State.description: Agent state. Any JSON value: the protocol carries state without interpreting it, so an object, an array, a string and a number are all valid.

delta.description: The change, as an RFC 6902 patch against the current state. Structural validity here does not mean the patch applies: a well-formed operation may point at a path that does not exist, which RFC 6902 leaves to the applier.

ag-ui-1_StateSnapshotEvent.description: Replaces the agent state wholesale. Sent when a delta cannot express the change, or to resynchronise a consumer.

ag-ui-1_StepStartedEvent.description: Opens a named step within a run, for producers whose frameworks have a step concept worth surfacing.

stepName.description: The step's name. Identifies it: the matching STEP_FINISHED carries the same name.

ag-ui-1_SubagentErrorEvent.description: Reports that a subagent invocation failed. The run may continue: a parent agent is free to handle a failed subagent, which is why this is not RUN_ERROR.

message.description: What went wrong, for a person to read.

code.description: A machine-readable error code. An open string.

ag-ui-1_SubagentFinishedEvent.description: Ends a subagent invocation's segment of this run, either because the work completed or because it is suspended awaiting outside input.

result.description: The subagent's return value, if it has one. Any JSON value, mirroring RUN_FINISHED.result.

outcome.description: Why the segment ended. Absent means success. A suspended subagent is neither a success nor a failure, which is why saying so needs its own value rather than being inferred from a later interrupt.

ag-ui-1_SubagentFinishedOutcome.description: Why a subagent's segment of a run ended. Mirrors RunFinishedOutcome one level down.

ag-ui-1_SubagentFinishedSuccessOutcome.description: The subagent completed its work. Equivalent to an absent outcome.

ag-ui-1_SubagentFinishedSuspendedOutcome.description: The subagent is paused awaiting outside input. Terminal for this stream, not for the subagent: a later run may continue the same invocation once the interrupts are answered.

interruptIds.description: The run-level interrupts this subagent raised itself. May be empty or absent: a subagent suspended because a descendant interrupted owns no interrupt of its own.

ag-ui-1_SubagentRunId.description: An opaque handle for one subagent invocation, not a reusable name for a subagent definition: two invocations of the same subagent carry two different values. Named to mirror runId one level down, the way the subagent's name mirrors agentId.

ag-ui-1_SubagentStartedEvent.description: Announces that a subagent invocation has begun. Everything the subagent produces afterwards is attributed by carrying its subagentRunId, so a consumer can group the work without replaying the stream. Composed from BaseEvent alone rather than Attributable, because here subagentRunId identifies the subagent rather than attributing the event to one; attribution to an enclosing subagent is parentSubagentRunId.

name.description: The subagent's name, which is reusable across invocations, unlike subagentRunId.

description.description: What this subagent is for, for a consumer to display.

parentSubagentRunId.description: The subagent invocation that spawned this one, for nested delegation. Absent means the parent agent spawned it directly.

parentToolCallId.description: The tool call that spawned this subagent, for the pattern where agents are exposed to a model as tools. Lets a consumer tie the subagent to the call without reading rawEvent.

parentMessageId.description: The message that held the spawning tool call.

ag-ui-1_TestOperation.description: Asserts that the value at path equals value. RFC 6902 section 4.6.

value.description: The value the target must equal. Any JSON value, including null.

ag-ui-1_TextMessageChunkEvent.description: A shorthand that stands in for a start, content and end sequence, for producers that cannot know in advance where a message begins. Every field is optional because a continuation chunk omits what has not changed; which message a field-less chunk continues is a sequence question the prose specification answers.

messageId.description: The message this chunk belongs to. Absent continues the message already open.

role.description: Who the message is from, on the chunk that opens it.

delta.description: The fragment to append. May be the empty string.

name.description: An optional display name for the author.

ag-ui-1_TextMessageContentEvent.description: Appends a fragment to a streamed text message.

messageId.description: The message this fragment belongs to.

delta.description: The fragment to append. May be the empty string: providers emit empty deltas as keep-alives and while a tool call is being decided, and rejecting them would kill runs that are working correctly.

ag-ui-1_TextMessageRole.description: The roles a streamed text message may take. Excludes tool, which is carried by TOOL_CALL_RESULT rather than streamed as text.

ag-ui-1_TextMessageStartEvent.description: Opens a streamed text message. The content arrives as TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT events and the message closes with TEXT_MESSAGE_END.

messageId.description: Identifies the message this stream builds, and ties the later content and end events to it.

role.description: Who the message is from. An absent role means assistant; that meaning is normative and stated in the prose, because a validator treats a default as documentation rather than as behaviour.

name.description: An optional display name for the author, for providers that distinguish several participants in one role.

id.description: Identifies this part within its message. Optional, and nothing reads it yet: reserved so that a streamed part can be matched to its entry in history once assistant messages carry parts too.

metadata.description: Extra information about this part. Unconstrained, as on the media parts. This is where a text search hit carries its source and title, rather than the protocol modelling a search-result part of its own.

ag-ui-1_TokenUsage.description: Token counts for one provider and model, in the protocol's own accounting: every count is either a total or a named part of one, so entries from different providers add up without double-counting. inputTokens and outputTokens are the totals; reasoningTokens, cachedInputTokens and cacheWriteInputTokens are parts of them, never additions to them; totalTokens is the two totals summed. Every field is a label or a number — nothing content-bearing or identifying, no prompts, completions, messages, or thread, run and user identifiers.

inputTokens.description: Every prompt token the call was charged for: tokens read from a provider cache, tokens written to one, and audio or other non-text input all count here. cachedInputTokens and cacheWriteInputTokens break this number down and are never added to it — a provider that reports its cache counts beside a smaller input count has them added in by the producer before the entry leaves. Bounded like timestamp and for the same reason: a count above the JSON safe-integer range does not survive a round trip, so a consumer would silently read a different number than the producer wrote.

outputTokens.description: Every generated token, reasoning included where the provider distinguishes it. reasoningTokens breaks this number down and is never added to it — a provider that reports reasoning tokens beside a smaller completion count has them added in by the producer.

totalTokens.description: inputTokens plus outputTokens, under the accounting above. A producer MAY compute it rather than copy a provider's total, and copies a provider's total only when that total counts the same way, so a consumer can read this field as the sum of the other two.

reasoningTokens.description: Output tokens spent on reasoning, where the provider distinguishes them. Part of outputTokens, not in addition to it.

cachedInputTokens.description: Input tokens read from a provider cache. Part of inputTokens, not in addition to it, and disjoint from cacheWriteInputTokens.

cacheWriteInputTokens.description: Input tokens written to a provider cache on this call, where the provider distinguishes them. Part of inputTokens, not in addition to it, and disjoint from cachedInputTokens. Its own field because providers price a cache write differently from a cache read, so a consumer computing cost cannot do without it.

ag-ui-1_Tool.description: A tool the agent may call.

name.description: The tool's name, as the agent will call it.

description.description: What the tool does, for the agent to decide when to use it.

parameters.description: A JSON Schema describing the tool's arguments. Carried opaquely: the protocol does not constrain or validate it. Optional, because all three SDKs already treat it that way and a tool that takes no arguments has nothing to declare; an absent schema and an empty one mean the same thing to an agent.

metadata.description: Extra information about the tool, for consumers that attach their own rendering or routing information to it.

ag-ui-1_ToolCall.description: A call an assistant message made. Carries no subagent attribution of its own and inherits its containing message's, since several calls can share one parent.

id.description: Identifies the call. The answering tool message carries this as its toolCallId.

type.description: The only kind of call the protocol models.

function.description: What is being called, and with what.

encryptedValue.description: A provider's opaque artefact belonging to this call.

metadata.description: Extra information attached to this call. Carried here rather than folded into the containing message, because several calls can share one parent and merging them would make the result depend on their order.

ag-ui-1_ToolCallArgsEvent.description: Appends a fragment of a tool call's arguments.

toolCallId.description: The call these arguments belong to.

delta.description: A fragment of the arguments, which concatenate into the call's argument text — conventionally a JSON document, though the protocol does not validate it (see FunctionCall.arguments). Deliberately a string rather than parsed JSON: a fragment is not itself a document. May be the empty string.

ag-ui-1_ToolCallChunkEvent.description: A shorthand that stands in for a tool call's start, args and end sequence. Every field is optional for the same reason as TEXT_MESSAGE_CHUNK.

toolCallId.description: The call this chunk belongs to. Absent continues the call already open.

toolCallName.description: Which tool is being called, on the chunk that opens it.

parentMessageId.description: The assistant message that holds this call.

delta.description: A fragment of the arguments. May be the empty string.

ag-ui-1_ToolCallEndEvent.description: Closes a tool call, meaning its arguments are complete.

ag-ui-1_ToolCallResultEvent.description: Carries what a tool returned. Mints a tool message rather than appending to an existing one, which is why it has its own messageId.

messageId.description: The tool message this result becomes.

content.description: What the tool returned: either plain text, or an ordered list of parts, exactly as on the tool message this event mints. A tool returning structured data serialises it into text; media travel as parts of their own.

role.description: Present only for symmetry with the message it mints; the value is fixed, so a producer may leave it out.

ag-ui-1_ToolCallStartEvent.description: Opens a tool call. The arguments arrive as TOOL_CALL_ARGS events and the call closes with TOOL_CALL_END.

toolCallId.description: Identifies the call, and ties the later args, end and result events to it.

parentMessageId.description: The assistant message that holds this call. Absent means the producer did not attribute it to one.

ag-ui-1_ToolMessage.description: What a tool returned, as a message in the conversation. Stands alone rather than composing BaseMessage, because it carries no name.

role.description: Fixed. Declared here rather than inherited, because this message does not compose BaseMessage.

content.description: What the tool returned: either plain text, or an ordered list of parts. A tool returning structured data serialises it into text; media travel as parts of their own.

error.description: Why the tool failed, when it did. Present alongside content rather than instead of it, so a partial result survives a failure.

encryptedValue.description: A provider's opaque artefact belonging to this message.

metadata.description: Extra information attached to this message.

ag-ui-1_UrlSource.description: Bytes referenced by URL, fetched by whoever needs them.

value.description: The URL. Deliberately not constrained to a URI format, so a scheme a producer already uses is not rejected here.

mimeType.description: What the resource is, when the producer knows. Optional, because the response can say.

ag-ui-1_UserMessage.description: A message from the person using the application.

content.description: What the person sent: either plain text, or an ordered list of parts for a multimodal message.

id.description: Identifies this part within its message. Optional, and nothing reads it yet: reserved as on the text part.

metadata.description: Extra information about this part. Unconstrained, as on the other media parts.

ai-sdk-ui.description: Exported from uiMessageChunkSchema of ai@7.0.113 by typescript/packages/host/scripts/export-ui-schemas.ts. Never edited by hand.
ai-sdk-ui.title: AI SDK UI message stream v1 chunk (ai@7.0.113)

api_ApiErrorCode.description: Typed failure codes public API calls return that the log never records. The wire ErrorCode enum (events.v1.schema.json) is what the log records. A public failure code is one of the two; add only.

events_AdapterRef.description: The model adapter and every provider-conversion setting that affects the wire request (API flavour, cache-breakpoint placement, tool-choice mapping). Part of Render v1 line 0.

events_ArtifactRef.description: Content-addressed bytes. The artifact is durable before any event references it; readers verify sha256 and length.

events_AudioPart.description: Recorded (non-realtime) audio, e.g. a channel voice note. Only adapters that declare audio input accept it; others fail pre-dispatch with content_unsupported. Realtime sessions are out of scope.

transcript.description: Host-produced transcript, shown only to adapters without audio input when the agent opts in.

events_BounceCode.description: Why a recipient refused pending mail: it was for an older generation, or the member ended.

events_Budget.description: Limits checked before every model_request. Unknown usage counts at its conservative upper bound.

events_CallId.description: Tool call id; may be provider-issued. The effect key is derived: <branch_id of the tool_call event>:<call_id>.

events_CitationPart.description: Annotates the text part immediately before it. source_id is a URL (web), doc_id (knowledge, with version), document artifact sha256 (document) or call_id (tool_result). ref and span name the exact cited bytes.

output.description: The latest task's answer; structured output is its accepted value as RFC 8785 JSON text.

events_EffectClass.description: read_only: no state change anywhere; no effect events. sandbox_local: changes only sandbox state; valid only under deny-all egress or enforced operation mediation. idempotent: the provider dedups on the effect key within dedup_window_ms. reconcilable: the adapter can look up the outcome with finality. unguarded: no contract; uncertainty always parks. Undeclared tools are unguarded.

events_Envelope.description: Fields common to every event. seq is contiguous along the branch's resolved chain. prev_hash is sha256 of the previous line's exact bytes (without newline) within the same branch segment; the first event of a segment chains to its header.

branch_id.description: The branch that wrote this event. Always the branch of the segment it is stored in.

critical.description: true: a reader that does not know (type, type_version) must refuse the log. false: it may skip the event.

epoch.description: Writer fencing epoch from the branch lease. Non-decreasing along the resolved chain.

event_id.description: Unique along the resolved chain (every ancestor segment plus this branch), checked on append and import (semantic rule 28).

events_ErrorCode.description: Pinned typed-error codes shared by both implementations. Add only; never rename after the first release.

observed_is_upper_bound.description: true when unknown usage was counted at its conservative upper bound.

owner_thread_id.description: Required exactly when scope is ancestor: the ancestor thread whose budget refused the reservation.

scope.description: Which budget refused the reservation. run and thread: this thread's own budget (the owner is the envelope thread_id, so owner_thread_id is absent). ancestor: a budget of an ancestor thread in the agent tree, named by owner_thread_id.

to_thread.description: The lead only: members can't hand off.

events_HostedToolPart.description: A provider-executed tool use and its result, inside one model attempt. The execution owner is the provider: it is never turned into a tool_call or dispatched locally. ref holds the exact provider blocks; readable citations follow as citation parts.

events_ImagePart.description: An image the model sees. Bytes are always an artifact; width and height are what the adapter needs for scaling (computer use coordinates).

events_InputPart.description: What a user or channel may send. No tool_use: user content never enters dispatch.

events_Int.description: JSON integer in the cross-language safe range.

events_InvalidDefinition.description: Why a start's chosen fields (label, instructions, tools, model) were refused: its invalid_definition detail.

allowed.description: With not_allowed on tools or model: the names the template allows.

events_JsonValue.description: Any validated JSON value (tool input, model params, MCP payloads). Numbers follow.

events_MailAddress.description: A member at one generation, or the team log (the operator's replies and notifications).

events_MailEnvelope.description: One mail, as the sender's message_sent records it and every receipt copies it byte for byte. member_parked is a one-time, non-consuming park notice.

ask_id.description: ask: its own mail_id. reply: the ask it answers. bounce: the open ask it closes as member_ended.

causal.description: The request or event that caused this mail: the call's tool_call, the operator_request, the member's idle or end event, or the refused mail's mail_refused.

monitor_id.description: The monitor this notification fires; its row is deleted in the same append.

result.description: member_settled (completed), member_ended (terminal), or an ask's bounce (the ended member's result).

events_MailId.description: <sender branch_id>:<call_id or request_id> for mail a call sends; <sender branch_id>:<event_id of the message_sent> for mail the runtime sends (notifications, bounces, lead-close cancels).

events_MailSender.description: The sending member, or the operator request. Written by the fenced writer; never an actor.

instructions.description: The written instructions, byte for byte: the member's line 0 ends with them in the delimited block. Absent: the preamble alone.

model.description: The chosen key of the template's models.

tools.description: The chosen tools, unique, in the template's pinned order; none of the framework set. The member pins exactly these and the framework tools.

events_MemberErrorCode.description: A failed member's code: the host API RunErrorCode, plus pin_unavailable and pin_mismatch for a failed rebind.

events_MemberName.description: <agent>-<k>, k counting that agent's members in the team from 1. The lead's name is its agent name.

events_MemberRef.description: One member of one team. Immutable.

generation.description: Changes only through a supervised restart; 1 until then.

events_ModelSettings.description: One settings epoch: everything in Render v1 line 0 except system and tools.

reasoning_carryover.description: keep: earlier reasoning and hosted_tool parts render as recorded. omit_prior: parts recorded before this epoch are omitted from later renders (a recorded decision, not a silent drop).

events_MonitorId.description: <watcher branch_id>:<event_id of the registering event>:<target name>; the target name is task for a start's task monitor. Derived, never generated.

events_ParkAddress.description: What a parked branch waits on; resumed must name the same address. For kind effect, id is the derived effect key; for kind child, the parked subagent's child_thread_id; for kind ask, the AskId; for kind wait, the WaitId; for kind member, the task MonitorId of the parked member.

events_PermissionRule.description: Tool(specifier) grammar. The tool part may end in * (mcp__github__*).

events_Policy.description: The resolved, secret-free runtime policy pinned at thread start (covered by config_hash, not model-visible). Each section is absent (the ADR defaults apply) or complete. ADRs 0019-0023.

budget.description: Thread-level budget. A run budget rides on the user_input that starts the run.

defer_threshold.description: Reserved: not read (no automatic deferral by size). Kept because existing logs pin it.

defer_tools.description: auto: tools marked defer are deferred; never: none; always: every app, extension and MCP tool without ends_turn. A child that doesn't set it pins its parent's.

max_pause_continuations.description: Re-requests after pause_turn responses in one turn before the turn ends with error. Absent means 3.

handoffs.description: Agent names this agent may hand the conversation to.

models.description: Every model this thread may use (primary and fallbacks), with its window, output cap and price. settings_changed may only name a listed model.

context_window.description: Maximum input tokens one request may carry (the factory's max_input_tokens).

input_billing_bound.description: context_window: the adapter declares that billed input units (input plus cache reads and writes) per attempt never exceed the context window. none: no bound is known, so a cost budget can't be enforced for this model (setup refuses it unless on_unknown_usage is stop).

price.description: Nano-currency units per token (USD 3 per million tokens = 3000).

output.description: Structured final output. schema_sha256 is the RFC 8785 hash of schema.

output_styles.description: Named instructions Thread.setOutputStyle can switch the thread to; an injected{source: output_style} must carry the text pinned here.

events_Principal.description: A verified identity, normalized by the host. issuer names the identity authority (e.g. slack:T024BE7LD, api), tenant the isolation scope.

events_Provenance.description: Causal, not structural: who originated the work and which request it belongs to. One turn's opening batch shares one (principal, root_request).

principal.description: The verified originating principal: the root run's input principal, or the operator's.

root_request.description: The lead run's user_input, or the team log's operator_request. Budgets roll up to its run budget.

via.description: The member hops. Provenance only: authority, credentials and grants never transfer.

events_ReasoningPart.description: Opaque provider continuation material (Anthropic thinking or redacted_thinking with its signature, OpenAI reasoning items with encrypted content). ref holds the exact provider bytes/JSON. Never rendered as text and never required in a UI. Render v1 emits the part as recorded; an adapter that cannot send it back fails with continuation_unsupported, never drops it silently. Only settings_changed{reasoning_carryover: omit_prior} omits earlier parts.

summary.description: Provider-supplied readable summary, for display only.

events_RequestId.description: One operator request: a team.start, send, ask, wait or cancel call.

events_RequestRef.description: An event in another thread's log, by thread and event id.

events_ResultPart.description: Ordered, mixed text and media of a tool result. No tool_use.

events_Span.description: Half-open range [start, end) in UTF-8 BYTE offsets of the referenced text or artifact bytes. Both ends fall on character boundaries. Python and TypeScript convert from their native string indices; a span never means code units.

events_StoredMemberResult.description: What a settled member returned, as member_idle, member_ended, notifications and member_observed record it. Public result APIs hydrate a ref'd output (sha256 and length verified); the audit feed returns it as stored.

events_TeamRefusal.description: A refusal an operator request records as operator_refused. A model call records its refusal in its own tool_result.

events_TextBody.description: Inline text up to the inline cap, else a content-addressed artifact written before the append.

events_TextOrContent.description: Exactly one of plain text or ordered input parts.

events_TextOrRef.description: Exactly one of inline text or an artifact ref.

events_Threshold.description: Absolute tokens, or a fraction of the effective context window in permille (850 = 85%). Integers only.

events_TimeMs.description: Unix epoch milliseconds. Informational; never used for ordering.

events_Tokens.description: A measured token count, or null when the provider did not report it (unknown, never zero).

dedup_window_ms.description: The provider's declared dedup window for this tool's effect key.

defer_loading.description: true: deferred. Render v1 shows only {name, description, deferred: true} until tool_search loads it: a tools_loaded naming its spec_ref, or (legacy inline form) a tools_changed with cause tool_search whose spec omits this flag. A call to a deferred tool fails pre-effect with tool_not_loaded.

ends_turn.description: A successful result ends the turn without another model call (the final_output tool).

input_schema.description: Required, except in the reference form (spec_ref), which has none.

origin.description: The extension that contributed this tool, static or from its setup. Not model-visible (not in Render v1 line 0); covered by config_hash.

output_schema.description: Optional JSON Schema for the tool's result value. A result that fails it is recorded as an error result; the effect still happened.

events_ToolUsePart.description: A locally dispatchable call proposed by the model. Only model_response and model_response_recovered may carry it; a tool_call must match one.

events_Usage.description: Per-field measured-or-unknown usage. input_tokens and output_tokens are always present and null when unknown (a stream that broke before its usage report). input_tokens excludes cache reads and writes; output_tokens includes reasoning tokens. A cache field is absent when the adapter's usage profile has no such billing category, and null when it has one but the value did not arrive.

events_Uuid.description: Lowercase UUID string. Writers MUST generate UUIDv7; readers accept any lowercase UUID, so the version is not an admission rule.

events_ev_agent_finished.description: The child's one terminal result (F7.5). Exactly once per agent_spawned.

usage.description: The child's aggregate usage; null fields are unknown.

events_ev_agent_spawned.description: A child thread was created for a spawn call. Durable before the child's thread_started, so cancellation and recovery can find it.

events_ev_answer_rejected.description: The asker's channel reply matched none of the open question's options (rule 49). The question stays open; the host derives the correction message from this event. Render v1 renders nothing for it.

call_id.description: The open ask_user call the reply was for.

events_ev_approval_granted.description: actor.principal is the approver, checked against current approver policy at consumption. challenge_id, call_id and args_hash must match the open challenge; the branch is the envelope branch_id.

events_ev_approval_requested.description: A single-use challenge bound to one invocation. The full binding (tenant, installation, file hashes) lives in the approvals table; args_hash is recorded because it is what the approver is shown.

events_ev_ask_closed.description: In the asker's log (a member, or the team log): closes the open ask. A member asker also appends resumed and the ask call's one tool_result.

outcome.description: Decided in order: a reply, then a member_ended bounce, then a cancel or team close, else the deadline.

reply.description: The reply mail, received in this same append; its text is the answer.

events_ev_budget_exceeded.description: A tree-wide budget reservation before a model_request failed. observed = settled usage of the whole tree under that budget plus the refused reservation. The run ends: pending calls close, then turn_completed{budget_exhausted}; no model_request follows until a new user_input.

observed_is_upper_bound.description: true when unknown usage was counted at its conservative upper bound.

owner_thread_id.description: Required exactly when scope is ancestor: the ancestor thread whose budget refused the reservation.

scope.description: Which budget refused the reservation. run and thread: this thread's own budget (the owner is the envelope thread_id, so owner_thread_id is absent). ancestor: a budget of an ancestor thread in the agent tree, named by owner_thread_id.

observed_is_upper_bound.description: true when unknown usage was counted at its conservative upper bound.

owner_thread_id.description: Required exactly when scope is ancestor: the ancestor thread whose budget refused the reservation.

scope.description: Which budget refused the reservation. run and thread: this thread's own budget (the owner is the envelope thread_id, so owner_thread_id is absent). ancestor: a budget of an ancestor thread in the agent tree, named by owner_thread_id.

events_ev_cancel_requested.description: Durable cancellation barrier; also the hard-stop control event. No dispatch happens after it.

events_ev_cancelled.description: Work stopped. Must not be written while any effect is unsettled; unsettled effects park instead.

events_ev_channel_delivery.description: One inbound item, appended when the run consumes it from the inbox. The inbox row (unique per item_key) was durable before the webhook response. item_key is the provider's per-item id, or <delivery_id>#<index> for batches without one. actor.principal is the mapped sender.

events_ev_compacted.description: Render replaces events from..to with the summary as untrusted reference. Both ends are step boundaries (no pending call, no open model attempt), so a tool pair is never split (semantic rule 10). The log is untouched, and the declared prefix (line 0) is never compacted. When summary_request_event_id is set, summary_ref is the UTF-8 text of that compaction request's response.

cause_event_id.description: The compaction_requested this answers (trigger manual). Required while a request is unanswered.

events_ev_compaction_failed.description: A compaction attempt failed. Consecutive failures since the last compacted open the circuit breaker (derived).

cause_event_id.description: The compaction_requested this answers (trigger manual). Required while a request is unanswered.

events_ev_compaction_requested.description: An operator asked for a compaction while the thread was idle (Thread.compact). The next run summarizes events from the first user_input to the one before this request, before its first turn request; the compacted or compaction_failed that names it (cause_event_id) answers it. Renders nothing.

instructions.description: Operator text for the summary; it follows the fixed instruction of the side request.

events_ev_context_edited.description: Changes how earlier tool results render, never the results themselves. clear replaces the call's result lines with the fixed placeholder; redact replaces spans of one text part (part 0 is the preview when there is no content) with [redacted]. Every call_id must have a recorded result.

request_event_id.description: reason provider only: the attempt whose effective context the provider edited, as the adapter reported it. That attempt's effective context is non-exact for replay.

events_ev_context_preflight_blocked.description: before any model_request exists, the context estimate reached the effective window, so no request was created, sent or billed. action compact runs the once-per-step reactive compaction; fail ends the turn context_exhausted. estimated_tokens is an estimate (rendered bytes / 4), labeled as such.

events_ev_effect_begin.description: Durable before dispatch. From the moment dispatch is accepted the effect is potentially sent until an effect_commit or effect_resolved settles it. A re-dispatch after safe_to_retry, not_sent or assume_not_done reuses the derived effect key with attempt+1.

events_ev_effect_resolved.description: Settles an unknown effect (C3). confirmed_success: the effect happened (final lookup or provider receipt). safe_to_retry: a re-send under the same key is deduplicated by the provider inside its window (by provider_dedup), or a lookup whose contract is final proved absence (by reconcile). not_sent: the adapter proves the request never left, or the provider confirmed cancellation with finality. interrupted: a sandbox_local process group was confirmed terminated. assume_*: an authorized human decision. An effect that stays unknown is parked, not resolved.

events_ev_effect_unknown.description: The outcome of a begun attempt is uncertain. Timeouts and transport errors after dispatch land here too, never in a plain error result.

events_ev_fork.description: First event of a child branch, right after the child's own header (prev_hash = sha256 of that header). The parent's rows are referenced, never copied. Derived, not stored: at_seq = this event's seq - 1; for reason snapshot the fork point is the parent's snapshot event at at_seq; the thread is the envelope thread_id.

at_hash.description: sha256 of the parent's line at at_seq. Binds the child to the parent's chain.

knowledge_policy.description: How the child searches knowledge. pinned (the API default): as of the fork snapshot's knowledge_revision. current: the live corpus. Recorded retrievals always replay as recorded.

reason.description: snapshot: a user fork at an eligible snapshot event. repair: operator repair of a corrupt parent at its last valid line; no sandbox is restored and the child is inspection-only (never runnable).

sandbox_id.description: The isolated child sandbox restored from the snapshot, with its manifest verified.

events_ev_handoff.description: The conversation moves to another agent's new thread. After it this thread takes no new input and no model_request; the host routes the conversation to to_thread_id.

events_ev_heartbeat.description: Reserved control event: wakes a model turn while only non-blocking tool calls are pending. Renders as a user line listing the running calls.

events_ev_hook_decision.description: A policy hook's decision, durable before any work it gates. Replay reads it and never re-runs the hook. failed means the hook threw or timed out: a gating hook's failure denies; an observation hook's failure changes nothing.

input_event_id.description: before_input: the user_input or steer decided on. A deny or failed decision means that input renders nothing. before_model_switch for a revert: the input that caused it.

events_ev_injected.description: Model-visible context not typed by the user. memory, knowledge, attachment, todo (the agent's own list), agent (child or teammate output) and handoff (forwarded history) are always untrusted_reference.

events_ev_log_repaired.description: Evidence of an import that dropped a torn tail (JSONL framing only; the SQLite store cannot tear). The dropped bytes are kept as an artifact.

events_ev_mail_refused.description: The recipient refused a pending mail (its row becomes stale for stale_member, returned for member_ended); a bounce to the sender goes in the same append.

events_ev_member_ended.description: The member's terminal result (failed, cancelled, budget_exhausted, or a lead's handed_off). Its append fires every monitor on this generation and refuses every pending inbound mail with a bounce. A lead's also closes the team and cancels every live member.

events_ev_member_idle.description: In the member's log, with the turn_completed that ends its task: the row becomes idle with this result, and each settle monitor and an unfired task monitor fires in the same append.

events_ev_member_observed.description: The waiter or monitor found its target already settled when it registered: recorded in the waiter's own log, with no mail and no monitor row.

result.description: Byte for byte the target's committed member_idle or member_ended result at source.

events_ev_member_started.description: In the starter's log (the lead, or the team log for an operator start), with the task's message_sent: inserts the member's row (starting), its task mail and the starter's task monitor.

budget.description: The member's own budget: the minimum of start's budget and the matching messagePolicy rule's.

config_hash.description: The pinned definition, whose canonical bytes are stored before this append; materialize rebinds against it.

define.description: Present exactly when the agent is a dynamic agent: what its starter chose. config_hash binds it.

label.description: A display name the starter gave (1-64 code points, no control or format characters; semantic rule 46). Never hashed, never rendered to a model.

parent.description: The structural parent the member's thread_started will carry: the lead's member_started, or the lead's thread_started for an operator start.

thread_id.description: The member's thread, opened at materialize (the starting window has no branch).

events_ev_message_policy_decided.description: Every team authorization decision, for model and operator alike, in the deciding writer's log.

rule.description: message_policy: the matching rule, by its from and to agents (unique per host), so a reordered policy still names it.

source.description: team: what the team grants (members send, ask, wait and monitor one another; the lead starts; a starter cancels). message_policy: a rule. default: default deny.

events_ev_message_received.description: The recipient consumed a mail (its row becomes consumed). Actor {host, provenance.principal}. It opens a turn only as the Teams rules say, and renders as an untrusted <message> user line.

envelope.description: Byte for byte the sender's message_sent envelope, provenance included, so every rule about received mail reads only this log.

events_ev_message_sent.description: Mail, in the sender's log: inserts its pending mail row (and for an ask, its open asks row).

events_ev_mode_changed.description: Permission mode change. from must be the current mode; to bypass needs policy.permissions.allow_bypass. Never caused by the agent alone: an operator via the host API, or an approved exit_plan_mode call (cause_event_id).

events_ev_model_attempt_abandoned.description: A model_request with no response. provider_outcome unknown means it may have been billed; a new attempt is a new model_request with attempt+1.

billing.description: not_billed only when provider_outcome is not_sent or the adapter's declared billing contract (in line 0 adapter settings) states this rejection class is not billed; a status code alone is not proof. Absent means unknown: the attempt is charged at its bound.

reason.description: rate_limited (429), overloaded (529), server_error (5xx or connection reset) and prompt_too_long are provider rejections: provider_outcome failed. guardrail: a parallel input guardrail denied.

events_ev_model_request.description: One model attempt, durable before dispatch (C2). request_ref holds the Render v1 bytes; req_hash is request_ref.sha256 (not stored twice) and is what the adapter guard checks. declared_prefix describes Render v1 line 0, which must be byte-equal on every request of the branch (C7).

attempt.description: 1 for a fresh request; n+1 when re-sending after model_attempt_abandoned.

cause_event_id.description: purpose compaction only: the compaction_requested this side request summarizes for. Its history is cut at that request (Render v1).

input_bound_tokens.description: A pre-dispatch upper bound on billed input units for this attempt, from the provider's token-counting API when the adapter supports it. Absent: the model's context_window bounds it.

purpose.description: turn (absent means turn) or compaction: the summarizer side request. A compaction request and its response render nothing into later requests.

events_ev_model_response.description: complete: the stream finished. partial: the stream broke after the listed complete parts; tool calls already recorded from it keep their ids and are not re-requested.

stop_reason.description: Only end_turn, stop_sequence and refusal complete a turn; tool_use dispatches; max_tokens continues; pause_turn re-requests with the paused content as-is, up to context.max_pause_continuations; context_window_exceeded ends the turn context_exhausted; other (a reason the adapter can't name) ends it error. Never success for the last two.

events_ev_model_response_recovered.description: A response recovered after a crash by adapter lookup (by the derived client request id <branch_id>:<model_request event_id>, or the provider request id) instead of re-sending. Written only when the lookup found the response with finality; not_found that is final becomes model_attempt_abandoned{provider_outcome: not_sent}, anything else is abandoned as unknown. Reduce and render treat it exactly like model_response.

stop_reason.description: Only end_turn, stop_sequence and refusal complete a turn; tool_use dispatches; max_tokens continues; pause_turn re-requests with the paused content as-is, up to context.max_pause_continuations; context_window_exceeded ends the turn context_exhausted; other (a reason the adapter can't name) ends it error. Never success for the last two.

events_ev_monitor_set.description: A model monitor on a member: an end monitor whose id is <branch_id>:<this event_id>:<member name>. Its member_ended mail opens a turn for an idle watcher.

events_ev_operator_refused.description: An operator request refused under the team-log writer. busy is never logged: no writer was acquired.

detail.description: Present exactly when code is invalid_definition, so a replayed request returns it.

events_ev_operator_request.description: One team.start/send/ask/wait/cancel call, in the team log, with the op's own events or its refusal in the same append.

body_hash.description: sha256 of the request's canonical JSON body.

idempotency_key.description: Scoped to this team and op; inserts the operator_receipts row.

provenance.description: root_request is this event: it is the root request for budgets.

events_ev_output_validated.description: Structured-output check of one candidate. source_event_id is the raw candidate: the final_output tool_call, or the model_response (native mode). accepted carries the validated value; rejected carries the errors shown to the model. schema_sha256 must equal policy.output.schema_sha256, and an accepted value must validate against that schema.

events_ev_park_escalated.description: A parked address outlived its TTL. The host notifies an approver; nothing is auto-resolved.

reason.description: awaiting_input: an ask_user question; the address is {kind: input, id: <call_id>}. awaiting_member: an open ask ({kind: ask}), a wait ({kind: wait}) or a parked run-owned member ({kind: member}).

events_ev_parked_data_reason.description: awaiting_input: an ask_user question; the address is {kind: input, id: <call_id>}. awaiting_member: an open ask ({kind: ask}), a wait ({kind: wait}) or a parked run-owned member ({kind: member}).

events_ev_permission_rule_added.description: A thread-scoped rule an approver chose while answering a challenge ('allow for this thread'). Checked after self-config, deny rules and protected paths, so it can never open those.

cause_event_id.description: The event that satisfied the address (approval, effect_resolved, user_input).

events_ev_retry_scheduled.description: A recorded wait before re-sending after a retryable rejection. Execution reads it: recovery after a crash waits only until not_before, and delay_ms counts toward max_total_wait_ms. So it is critical. The transient stream status during the wait is not logged.

events_ev_schedule_fired.description: occurrence_id is <schedule_id>@<scheduled instant, RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds>. The occurrence's schedule_occurrences row is decided in this event's append transaction, so two schedulers start one run.

timezone.description: IANA zone; UTC when the schedule omits one.

events_ev_schedule_skipped.description: An occurrence that was reserved but not run: missed (it fell due while no host ran), overlap (the schedule's previous run was still going) or removed (its agent is no longer served, or now pins another config than the thread was started with). Skipping it cannot change reduce or render output.

events_ev_settings_changed.description: Starts a new settings epoch: Render v1 line 0 takes model, params and adapter from here, system and tools stay pinned. C7 holds within each epoch. Never while a model attempt awaits its response. model must be listed in policy.models when policy is present.

actor.description: reason user: an operator principal, as actor user or host (the host API acting for that principal); the host still authorizes the principal, the schema only proves one is named. reason fallback, escalation or revert: automatic, so actor host or recovery only. Never model or tool.

events_ev_snapshot.description: A completed sandbox capture of the state after every event before this one. Appended only after the provider reports it durable and restorable. The event itself is the fork point.

knowledge_revision.description: The host knowledge store revision at capture. Present when the thread has a knowledge binding. A fork with knowledge_policy pinned searches as of this revision.

manifest_hash.description: RFC 8785 hash of the captured file-tree manifest (path, mode, size, sha256).

quiesced.description: How sandbox processes that could mutate captured state were handled. excluded lists only processes the provider proves cannot write captured paths.

knowledge_revision.description: The host knowledge store revision at capture. Present when the thread has a knowledge binding. A fork with knowledge_policy pinned searches as of this revision.

manifest_hash.description: RFC 8785 hash of the captured file-tree manifest (path, mode, size, sha256).

quiesced.description: How sandbox processes that could mutate captured state were handled. excluded lists only processes the provider proves cannot write captured paths.

events_ev_steer.description: Reserved control event: new user input that arrives while a turn is open. It does not open a turn; it renders as a user line at the next model request and may preempt an in-flight model attempt (that attempt is then model_attempt_abandoned{reason: steered}).

events_ev_stop_when_idle.description: Reserved control event: finish in-flight work (model attempt, pending calls, deferred results), start nothing new, then stop. A hard stop is cancel_requested.

events_ev_team_message.description: An addressed message between members. message_id is unique; delivery into a member's thread is injected{source: agent, origin.id: message_id}, deduplicated by that id.

to.description: A member id, or * for every member.

events_ev_team_opened.description: The team log's first event, in place of thread_started: opened in the lead's first append. The team log never renders to a model, never parks and never opens a turn.

events_ev_team_task_claimed.description: Atomic claim: the task exists, is open and unclaimed, and every blocker is completed.

events_ev_team_task_created.description: A shared team task, in the team lead's log (the one writer for team state).

events_ev_team_task_updated.description: completed and failed close a claimed task; released returns it to the open pool.

events_ev_thread_started.description: Pins everything in Render v1 line 0 (the declared immutable prefix) for the thread.

config_hash.description: sha256 of the RFC 8785 bytes of the resolved, secret-free agent config.

instructions.description: The full pinned system text: base instructions, extension instructions in order, skill listing, memory guidance.

model_params.description: Every adapter-visible generation parameter (max_tokens, temperature, tool_choice, ...).

parent.description: Set on a child thread: the parent event that created it (agent_spawned, handoff, or for a team member the lead's member_started, or the lead's thread_started for an operator-started member).

team.description: Set on the thread of an agent defined with team (a lead). Its first append also opens the team log and inserts the teams row and the lead's team_members row (role lead, generation 1).

log_branch_id.description: The team log's branch, opened in this append's transaction with its team_opened.

log_thread_id.description: The team log's thread, opened in this append's transaction with its team_opened.

events_ev_todos_updated.description: The agent's complete todo list after a todo_write call (F8). reduce keeps the latest. ids are unique.

events_ev_tool_call.description: A schema-validated call, durable before authorization and dispatch. input is the parsed args exactly. Derived, not stored: args_hash = sha256(RFC 8785 of input); effect_class and dedup_window_ms from the pinned ToolSpec named name; effect key = <this event's branch_id>:<call_id>. request_event_id lets a streamed call be recorded before its model_response.

events_ev_tool_result.description: Without content, preview is exactly what the model sees (one text part). With content, the model sees exactly those ordered parts and preview is a plain-text rendering for logs and channels. ref holds the full output when it exceeds the spill threshold. origin deferred is a placeholder for a non-blocking call whose real result arrives later as tool_result_late. origin answered is an ask_user answer and carries the answering principal.

events_ev_tool_result_late.description: Reserved: the real result of a non-blocking call, appended after its deferred placeholder and possibly after later turns. History is never rewritten; the placeholder stays.

events_ev_tools_changed.description: The model-visible tool set changed mid-thread (for example an MCP server's tool list). tools is the complete new set; tools_hash is sha256 of its RFC 8785 bytes.
