It renders as a line after the declared prefix, so line 0 stays equal (C7) while the log still records exactly what the model saw (C6). Later calls derive effect_class and dedup_window_ms from the latest set.

cause.description: Provenance. tool_search: the call whose result loaded deferred tools (those specs lose defer_loading). mcp_list_changed: a server's list changed. Absent means host.

events_ev_tools_loaded.description: Deferred tools a tool_search call loaded, each by the spec_ref it was pinned with. Appended in the same batch as that call's tool_result, right after it. It renders as a history line with the loaded specs read from their artifacts, so line 0 never changes; the tools stay loaded for the rest of the chain.

code.description: Only with reason error: the request needed a part the model doesn't declare (content_unsupported) or another provider's continuation (continuation_unsupported), found before any model_request; or the adapter refused the send because its transport bypasses the fence (transport_fence_unsupported, never retried); or the response held a registered secret in provider material that is replayed byte-exact and so can't be redacted (secret_in_provider_output: nothing of it is stored, never retried); or a team member's rebind failed before its first model request: its definition, a tool or a model is not registered here (pin_unavailable), or the rebuilt config_hash differs (pin_mismatch).

events_ev_user_input.description: Opens a turn. actor.principal is the verified sender.

budget.description: The budget of the run this input starts.

client_message_id.description: The id a web UI gave this message (the AI SDK UIMessage id or the AG-UI message id), recorded by the UI routes so a retry finds its run and a snapshot names the message as the client does. Not rendered.

delivery_event_id.description: The channel_delivery or schedule_fired event this input came from.

mail_id.description: Exactly with source team_task: the task mail this input consumes (its row becomes consumed in this append).

events_ev_wait_finished.description: Closes a wait: deletes every remaining settle monitor with this wait_id. Settlement is by commit order, never by timestamps.

timed_out.description: true only when the deadline passed with the mode unmet.

events_ev_wait_started.description: A wait on members, in a member's log or the team log. A member waiter also parks {kind: wait, id: wait_id}.

members.description: Frozen at the call. Each gets a settle monitor <branch_id>:<this event_id>:<name>, or a member_observed.

mode.description: all, any, or the number of members that must settle.

events_ev_woken.description: Opens a turn for background results that arrived while no turn was open and no cancel barrier stood. Written only in the append that records those results, never retroactively. Renders nothing: the late results render.

causes.description: The tool_result_late events in this same append that woke the thread.

202.description: The user_input is durable; the run proceeds in the host. A replay under the same Idempotency-Key returns this same receipt. Follow the run with its events stream.

parameters.name: run_id
parameters.description: From RunAccepted: the run's user_input event_id.

parameters.name: after_seq
parameters.description: Resume after this seq (also accepted as the SSE Last-Event-ID). Default 0.

200.description: Server-sent events of one run. Each message's data is one SseMessage; committed events carry their seq as the SSE id, and the last message is the result naming run_id. Subscribing takes no input and starts nothing; it reads the log, it is not a second loop.
Visible branches (a forking branch is not listed).

201.description: The child branch, ready and runnable.

post.description: The authenticated principal must have approval authority under the ROOT run's approver set (spec/schema/README.md, Approval authority): the configured approvers, else the root run's originating principal. A descendant's challenge reached through the descendant thread's route is decided under the same root set. Otherwise 403 forbidden and nothing is appended.

Accepts duplicate risk, so it needs approval authority under the ROOT run's approver set, as decideApproval does; otherwise 403 forbidden and nothing is appended. The accepting principal is recorded as effect_resolved's actor.principal.

200.description: The AI SDK UI message stream (header x-vercel-ai-ui-message-stream: v1) of the run the request starts, retries or resumes, ended by data: [DONE]. A last user message starts a run on the key's thread (idempotent on its id); a last assistant message only records its approval decisions and ask_user answers and streams the resumed run. Frames are derived from the log (spec/schema/ui/README.md); each log-derived frame's SSE id is <seq>:<k>.

204.description: An assistant-last request with nothing to record and no run to stream.

200.description: useChat({resume: true}): the key's latest run, from its start, while it has not ended.

204.description: No active stream: the latest run has ended, or the key has no thread.

200.description: AG-UI 1.0 events of the run the input starts, retries or resumes. A stream that does not start at the run's first event is a replay and opens with MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT. An approval or a question ends it with RUN_FINISHED{outcome: interrupt}, answered by the next input's resume.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Resume after this frame id <seq>:<k> (also accepted as the SSE Last-Event-ID, which wins). AI SDK resumes with frame k+1 of event seq; AG-UI resumes at the event boundary after seq with a new RUN_STARTED and a snapshot.

200.description: For custom clients: the run's committed frames only, in the protocol's stream format, resumable by cursor. No live text.

get.description: A provider's subscription check (WhatsApp's hub.challenge): the query goes to the adapter's challenge, which verifies its token. Not authenticated by bearer. A channel whose adapter has no challenge is not_found.

404.description: Unknown channel, or one without a challenge.

post.description: Channel intake. The raw bytes and headers go to the adapter's verify; the whole batch is inserted into the inbox in one transaction before the adapter's ack response is returned. Not authenticated by bearer: the adapter verifies the provider's signature.

200.description: The adapter's ack (status, headers and body are the adapter's).
